name: KCC-20 reference actor at 10 token inputs / 10 outputs (La-Gauffre/KaspaRocket-Silverscript-Contract 86fe1e8e, kcc20.sil)

review.note: KaspaRocket's token program (kasparocket.fun), on mainnet since 2026-10-20 (first token 147dff25... at DAA 571,149,299) and on testnet-10: kcc20.sil at La-Gauffre/KaspaRocket-Silverscript-Contract 86fe1e8e (sha256 ba4403ed953dbb81023ffcd3723112a423dc23e2d7beeeb04556722d70e66321, headed 'Generated by argentc'), reviewed 2026-10-22 from its source, chain bytes, an instruction alignment against the reference actor kascov reviewed on 2026-10-21 (pin 9703112e, argent-lang/kcc20-reference c8a0871) and the real engine. Source: the file differs from the reference's generated sil/KCC20.sil in seven lines and nothing else: MAX_DELEGATES 2 to 9, MAX_TOKEN_OUTPUTS 3 to 10, gen__const_kcc20_suffix_len 0x2d0f0000 to 0x302c0000 (3,885 to 11,312), require(delegates_count <= 9), the delegate read loop bound 9, require(output_count <= 10) and the successor loop bound 10. KCC-20 section 2 lets a non-default configuration override the maximum token inputs and outputs and says the program artifact MUST describe them, and section 3 says each KCC-20 covenant MUST publish that artifact; the repository at that commit publishes no artifact JSON and no .ag source (README.md, kcc20.sil, LP_AMM.sil, Escrow_buy_token.sil, Escrow_sell_token.sil), and its README states the limits in prose. This pin is kascov's own description of the build, read from bytes, not an artifact its publisher released, so it records the artifact as unpublished: kascov cannot check what that artifact would say, and gives the build no conformance verdict either way (the API serves conformant null, not false). Not assessed is not a departure, and nothing below depends on it. Source to bytes: silverc built from silverscript 3ed973335b59269293564805cc2c58a14595ec03 (silverscript-lang 1.0.0, the revision c8a0871's Cargo.lock pins through argent 9a9f4b10) first reproduces c8a0871's artifact KCC20 bytecode byte for byte, window included (4,031 B, sha256 abcf7ae9...), then compiles kcc20.sil with zero constructor arguments to 11,458 B (sha256 678e203c6720abc70db0ce63c46a50e8ca33c6215a0f11a65b1f29f88482eba4: prefix 1, window 145, suffix 11,312) whose TemplateHash recomputes to ff3ae732 in Python and in kcc1::template_hash; two runs are byte-identical. Bytes to chain: no chain cell equals that compile byte for byte, because each carries its own state in the window [1,146); outside the window, every reveal below is the compile byte for byte. The fixtures are mainnet leader reveals (tag 79c71c23). A is 71b6c6af668cd81d859e1121c84580fce4d7434b4dbd520663896267511ebe50:0, the genesis cell of ROCKET (covenant 7cf4b45e...), revealed by 427214fd06202cd9302638411e751641efa2015ed3f8933756d6e97305e65edc input 0: 1,000,000,000 base units owned by the deployer's key (p2pk). B is 9f1be1022db2cf7b9bcf7a8caaa3fd0507a717b4fe6f4c9a8df70c344e03067d:2, a ROCKET cell of 633,030,484 owned by its market covenant a11ebeb4... (scheme 0x04), revealed by b5d073a616d79d27eb1d372ab4734032411c9ee94bd1a584ce0600681c1a1657 input 1, a transfer with three delegates, one more than the reference admits. Each is the last push of its spending signature script and its blake2b is the P2SH commitment it spent. A sweep of every spent covenant output on the 2026-10-21 copies (mainnet processed DAA 571,918,850, testnet-10 602,749,952) found 196 reveals of this build in 9 covenants on mainnet and 788 in 75 on testnet-10, each the compiled program byte for byte outside its window, each recomputing ff3ae732 and carrying it as window field 0; every successor a leader declared (267 on mainnet, 1,204 on testnet-10) rebuilds to its output's commitment. No reveal carries ff3ae732 in its own window without being this program. The only other programs that name it are larger ones (KaspaRocket's 41,918 B market on both networks, and testnet-10 programs of 41,922 B, 81.6 KB and 156.7 KB not identified here), each carrying this program's 11,312-byte suffix verbatim and naming one token covenant of this build. Read-only probes of the live mainnet database at 2026-10-21 21:00Z re-checked the P2SH of every spent cell of the 20 covenants of this build then (587). The window, as in the reference, is the actor's own template hash (gen__kcc20_template, one 32-byte push at R[1..34]) followed by the 112-byte KCC20State (R[34..146]), so the record sits at offset 33; the canonical hash is taken around the whole window and the record view around the record alone (3d689d62...), both required. fixtures_share_class: the build has many launches (9 on the mainnet copy, 75 on testnet-10's), not one, and the pair shares its class because every cell of this build on either network carries the all-zero class (857 on mainnet at 2026-10-21 21:00Z, 1,279 on testnet-10), so no two chain cells differ there. The window's end is proven from the program's own bytes instead: 11,458 is pushed ten times and -11,312 ten times (one pair per output slot, where the reference pushes 4,031 and -3,885 three times), 11,312 twice (0x302c0000, the suffix length that cuts a delegate's and a leader's program), and every continuation is rebuilt from the active input's own signature script as R[0..1] and the 11,312-byte suffix around a state the program encodes itself. Alignment: rebuilding the zero-window compile from the reference actor's bytes with only these edits reproduces it exactly (sha256 678e203c...): six bound opcodes (Op2 to Op9 at 276, 293 and 6259; Op3 to Op10 at 6216, 7078 and 8685), the two suffix-length pushes (3,885 to 11,312, at 254 and 10773), the two self-location constants in each copy of the successor rebuild (4,031 to 11,458 and -3,885 to -11,312), and the four unrolled loops repeated with byte-identical bodies (delegate read 2 to 9 copies of 657 B, delegate sum 2 to 9 of 89 B, successor checks 3 to 10 of 113 B, successor rebuild 3 to 10 of 202 B; a body carries no position constant, its index lives on the stack). After alignment 50 bytes differ and every one is on that list; no byte is unexplained. Every other instruction is the reviewed actor's, byte for byte, so the reference pin's instruction reading holds here with the bounds below. KCC20.transfer (79c71c23): the leader is the family's first input; up to nine delegates, each authenticated as this template by its P2SH and its template hash and required to carry the leader's extension commitment; one to ten family outputs, all authorised by the leader and equal in number to next_states; every successor amount non-negative, owner scheme 0x00-0x04, borrow scheme 0x00-0x03 and the leader's extension commitment; the input total equal to the output total in checked i64; a first witness byte 0x00 for owner authorization or 0x01 for a borrowed receive, any other refused. Owner arms: 0x00 CheckSig by the owner key; 0x01 a 32-byte key whose unkeyed BLAKE3 is the owner, then its signature (97 bytes exactly); 0x02 the same with a 33-byte ECDSA key (98 bytes); 0x03 the input named by a one-byte index spends the version-0 P2SH of the owner; 0x04 an input carrying the owner as its covenant id is present (empty witness); 0x05-0xff refused. Borrowed receive: scheme 0x00 refused; 0x01 an empty witness and a threshold read as the guard's first 8 bytes as a signed int, clamped to 0 when negative; 0x02 CheckSig by the guard key; 0x03 a 129-byte witness whose BLAKE3(next || one-time key) equals the guard, the key signing and next becoming the successor's guard; any other scheme refused; successor 0 keeps the owner, owner scheme, borrow scheme and class, carries the expected guard, grows by strictly more than the threshold and keeps at least the input's KAS. transfer_delegator (fd3ef14a): not the leader, at least two family inputs, no outputs of its own, the leader authenticated as this template, its own owner authorized as above without a path byte. Any other tag ends in OP_RETURN. Engine: crates/kascov-labkit/src/kcc20_kasparocket.rs runs the reference ladder on fixture A's chain bytes on the real Kaspa script engine with the covenant context (rusty-kaspa 98a4ccd), every input under the node's committed-budget limit. Every check the reference ladder attributes for the KCC20 actor was located in these bytes (184 verify sites, each asserted before it is patched) and attributed again by ablation, at every delegate slot and every output slot. The ladder's 328 report rows say exactly what that covers: 202 checks attributed (the shape is refused, and with the check ablated it passes on every input), 3 attributed at the one input in question, 14 members of redundant groups (each ablated alone still refuses, so the group is attributed together), 4 that the engine itself backs once ablated, 41 always-true guards (ablated, every accept shape still passes, so there is nothing for them to refuse), 11 rules the engine enforces with no instruction of their own to ablate, and 53 notes, accept cases, reader comparisons and chain re-runs. Nine delegates (ten token inputs) and ten outputs are accepted on every input; a tenth delegate and an eleventh output are refused, each bound by three redundant checks ({278, 295, 6261} and {6218, 7080, 8687}): each ablated alone still refuses, and all three ablated let a tenth delegate's amount vanish or an eleventh output of 1,000,000 pass. Conservation (8216) refuses one unit off at each of the ten outputs, in both directions, with no delegates and with nine. Also run: all five owner schemes as leader and as delegate, all four borrow schemes, the delegator at input 9 checking its leader, a fabricated 11,458-byte leader (refused), overflowing totals (refused by the engine) and a negative input amount (accepted as leader, F11 of the reference audit, as there). The engine re-ran the leader input of five mainnet ROCKET spends, each under its own signature script and committed budget, and accepted every one: b5d073a6 and c6f9741d (three delegates each), 853d2ffc (two), 4cb081a3 (one) and e841555c (none). Those leaders are cells owned by ROCKET's market covenant (scheme 0x04), so their verdict hangs on no signature. Only the leaders were re-run: not their delegates, and not testnet-10's two ten-input merges (a leader and nine delegates each), because those p2pk inputs' signatures commit to transaction data the index does not keep; they were checked byte for byte and by the reader instead. Largest shape (a leader, nine delegates, ten outputs, synthetic): the leader uses 1,356,890 script units (budget 135) and each delegate 203,880 (budget 20), and one budget unit less is refused; 118,070 B, compute mass 154,630, transient 472,280 and storage 181,500 at 1 KAS cells, within mainnet's post-Toccata block limits; the heaviest witnesses (a hash-chain borrowed leader, p2pkh-ecdsa delegates) measure 118,441 B, compute 155,001 and transient 473,764 (crates/kascov-labkit/tests/kr_align_limits.rs). kascov's check_family agreed with the engine on all ten synthetic shapes tried at these bounds, and under this pin reads the mainnet transfer b5d073a6 and the testnet-10 ten-input merge 30392428 with no violation; under the reference pin's 3/3 bounds it flags both. Genesis and issuance: the build has no issuer actor and no mint or burn entry, so issuers is empty on purpose. A token's supply is what its genesis transaction declares in the one covenant output it creates, which is this program itself (every KaspaRocket launch: 1,000,000,000 base units owned by a one-off deployer key, moved within seconds to the launch's market covenant); KCC-20 does not constrain what a genesis declares. The build is not exclusive to KaspaRocket's app: three testnet-10 tokens without a KaspaRocket payload use it too, so this pin names the build, never a token's venue. Not claimed: signature validity stays consensus's; KaspaRocket's market and escrow programs, and the larger programs above, are not described here. How kascov reads tokens of this build: from the genesis group forward, through the programs this pin describes only. A token whose genesis kascov cannot prove stays unvalidated, never verified: a genesis output no spend has revealed yet stays dark until its first spend, and a cell whose state kascov does not read proves nothing. kascov reads the canonical encodings KCC-1 asks of a spender, and a reveal in any other encoding is not read, so its token reads unvalidated, never invalid (F3 of the reference audit; that it holds here too is inferred from the instruction alignment above, which leaves that code byte for byte the reference's, and was not re-run on this build). A token of this build is shown as a KCC-20 token only once it is verified; until then kascov names the build as reviewed and says the token is not proven yet.
